summary: Forest Service lookout on Haystack Mountain, Jefferson County, MT: an L-4 cab built 1936, destroyed 1977. A footing and scattered wood remain near the trail's summit.

facts.status_note: Cab destroyed in 1977. A footing and scattered wood remain at the summit.

access.note: National Recreation Trail on Forest Service land; closed year-round to motorized travel.

visit.trail_note: About 3 to 3.6 miles, climbing just over 2,000 feet, per a county write-up and the trail listing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page dates a camp to 1911 and a platform to 1920. The 2015 photo page agrees on the 1920 platform and the 1936 cab. The 1936 newspapers describe a station completed that year, which fits the 1936 cab.
The November 1936 report calls the peak Lookout Mountain; the later reports call the station Haystack. The story treats them as one station.
The county write-up says about three miles; the trail listing says 3.6 miles. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 4.3 (14 ft) matches the 14-foot cabin in the 1936 report and the 14 x 14-foot cab in the county write-up. Those are cab sizes, not a tower height, so the field may need review. Record kind 'ground' matches the FFLA list, but the county write-up calls it a tower and the photo page calls the remains a footing. Rex's page says 19 miles northeast of Butte; the trail listing says 12 miles north. Elevations vary: 8,000 ft in the 1936 report, 8,819 to 8,821 ft in later pages. Five sources agree on the 1936 and 1977 dates.
